correctness.rationale: For known continuous F0, PIT yields iid uniform sample. Symmetric Watson kernel is degenerate with constant diagonal 1/12, killing diagonal covariance; an exactly integrated centered Brownian-bridge cross kernel 1/72 and count of 2n(n−1) matched ordered offdiagonal index pairs prove Cov=(n−1)/(36n) for every n≥1. Analytic beta-log moments give Var AD=[4−π²/3+2(n−1)(π²/3−3)]/n, and Watson quadratic polynomial gives Var U=(n−1)/(360n), yielding monotonic correlation and finite limit for n≥2. Embedded stand-alone verifier reproduces exact polynomial coefficients and test-value simulations; simulations are not used for the theorem.

originality.rationale: The new exact Watson–Anderson–Darling finite-n mixed covariance and its strictly monotone correlation require a genuinely new cross-kernel contraction. Inspected Stephens 1974 full text has individual spectral components, separate moments and power comparisons, while inspected Hwang–Kuriki 2024 full text gives generalized individual process covariance kernels; neither inspected set of results states or implies the exact mixed moment without additional calculation. A published composite-null tabulation and the historical Durbin–Knott components paper were treated as different/uncertain, respectively. Pairwise covariances of both tests with Cramér–von Mises would constrain, but cannot algebraically determine, the independent Watson–Anderson–Darling covariance entry. This PASS is an evidence-based no-coverage judgment, not uniqueness certification.

value.rationale: Watson removes an empirical circular-shift mode while Anderson–Darling emphasizes distribution tails. These are canonical competing checks of a known simple null. Their exact cross-null covariance is a natural missing structural dependence parameter for interpreting both checks; it is not determined by their individual variances or respective covariances with a third test. The sign, closed all-n value and strict sample-size monotonicity ending at a nonzero universal correlation quantify this relationship. No claim is made about constructing new combined-test critical values.
